ledger.note: 6000 BCE: the Jōmon hunter-gatherers hold the Japanese archipelago in the Initial Jōmon ("Initial (8,500-5,000 BC)"; the period began c. 14,000 BC).
5000 BCE: the Early Jōmon begins: "Early (5,000-3,520 BC)"; "The Early Jōmon period saw an explosion in population".
3520 BCE: the Middle Jōmon begins: "Middle (3,520-2,470 BC)"; the Sannai Maruyama settlement in Aomori is at its height (Sannai Maruyama page: occupied "(3900 - 2200 BCE)").
2470 BCE: the Late Jōmon begins: "Late (2,470-1,250 BC)".
1250 BCE: the Final Jōmon begins: "Final (1,250-500 BC)"; after 1500 BCE "populations seem to have contracted dramatically".

notes: Jōmon period of the Japanese archipelago; the page says 'the time between c. 14,000 and 300 BC' and the lead table gives Incipient 13,750-8,500, Initial 8,500-5,000, Early 5,000-3,520, Middle 3,520-2,470, Late 2,470-1,250, Final 1,250-500 BC; 'Recent findings have refined the final phase of the Jōmon period to 300 BC' (so the table's 500 and the 300 disagree, 300 used); a second list on the page gives Initial 7500-4000 BCE (not used). It began eight millennia before the project's first year; the dossier starts at -6000, in the Initial Jōmon. This dossier runs far beyond the 3400 BCE horizon on purpose: nothing else draws Japan until Cliopatria's Asuka Japan (540 CE). Extent: the page says the archipelago 'can be divided into 3 regions' (Honshu and Kyushu; Okinawa and the Ryukyu Isles; Hokkaido and Northern Tohoku), sites 'range from Hokkaido to the Ryukyu Islands', 'the population was concentrated in Honshu and Kyushu' and the Jōmon were 'mostly absent' from the Ryukyus; no population figure and no area. The shape is Japan without the Ryukyus (confidence 2). The Sannai Maruyama page (Aomori, '3900 - 2200 BCE', '40-hectare', '648 pit dwellings', jade traded from Niigata) shows the north of Honshu densely settled in the Early-Middle Jōmon. End: in Hokkaido and northern Tohoku the Jōmon were succeeded by 'the related people of the Zoku-Jomon' (Epi-Jōmon), elsewhere by the Yayoi ('c. 300 BCE - AD 300'; 'started between 500 and 300 BC according to radio-carbon evidence'). Neither has a dossier (counterparts), so Japan is blank from 299 BCE to Asuka Japan (540 CE) unless one is written. No area figure.
